title: The Cop and the Anthem
author: O. Henry
summary: 寒风凛冽的深秋，流浪汉苏比千方百计想被警察抓进温暖的岛上监狱过冬，却屡屡碰壁落空。当他在教堂听到庄严的赞美诗决心重新做人时，一只手搭在了他的肩上……

paragraphs.en: On his bench in Madison Square Soapy moved uneasily. When wild geese honk high of nights, and when women without sealskin coats grow kind to their husbands, and when Soapy moves uneasily on his bench in the park, you may know that winter is near at hand.
paragraphs.zh: 在麦迪逊广场的长凳上，苏比不安地挪动着身子。当大雁在夜空中高声悲鸣，当没有海豹皮大衣的妻子对丈夫变得温柔体贴，当苏比在公园的长凳上辗转难眠时，你就该明白，寒冬已迫在眉睫了。

paragraphs.en: A dead leaf fell in Soapy's lap. That was Jack Frost's card. Jack is kind to the regular denizens of Madison Square, and gives fair warning of his annual call. At the door of the park he hands his pasteboard to the North Wind.
paragraphs.zh: 一片枯叶飘落在苏比的膝头上。那是霜冻老人拜访的名片。霜冻老人对麦迪逊广场的常客一向仁慈，每年造访前都会发出友善的警告。在公园门口，他把请帖郑重地交给了北风。

paragraphs.en: Soapy's ambitions were not of the highest. In them there were no considerations of Mediterranean cruises or soporific Southern skies. Three months on the Island was what his soul craved. Three months of assured board and bed and congenial company, safe from Boreas and bluecoats.
paragraphs.zh: 苏比的雄心壮志绝非高不可攀。在他的愿望里，绝没有地中海巡航，也没有南国慵懒的碧空。在布莱克威尔岛上的监狱度过三个月，才是他灵魂深处的渴望。三个月有吃有住、远离刺骨北风和巡警骚扰的安全庇护所。

paragraphs.en: For years the hospitable Island had been his winter quarters. Just as his more fortunate fellow New Yorkers had bought their tickets to Palm Beach, Soapy had made his humble arrangements for his annual hegira to the Island.
paragraphs.zh: 多年来，那座好客的小岛一直是他的冬季度假胜地。正如家境更优渥的纽约客早早订好了前往棕榈滩的船票一样，苏比也早已为自己一年一度前往海岛的“圣迁”做好了朴素的安排。

paragraphs.en: There were many easy ways of doing this. The pleasantest was to dine luxuriously at some expensive restaurant; and then, after declaring a failure of money, be quietly and without uproar handed over to a policeman. A polite magistrate would do the rest.
paragraphs.zh: 达到这一目的有许多轻松门径。最惬意的一招，莫过于在某家奢华高档的餐馆里美餐一顿；酒足饭饱后坦白身无分文，然后不吵不闹地被交到巡警手里。剩下的，就全由通情达理的法官来判决了。

paragraphs.en: Soapy left his bench and strolled out of the square and across the level sea of asphalt, where Broadway and Fifth Avenue flow together. Up Broadway he turned, and halted at a glittering cafe, where are gathered together nightly the choicest products of the grape, the silkworm and the protoplasm.
paragraphs.zh: 苏比离开长凳，信步走出广场，穿过百老汇与第五大道交汇处平坦宽阔的沥青马路。他拐上百老汇，在一家灯火辉煌的咖啡餐馆前驻足，那里每晚汇聚着葡萄藤、蚕丝与人类原生质最顶级的结晶。

paragraphs.en: Soapy had confidence in himself from the lowest button of his vest upward. He was shaven, and his coat was decent and his neat black tie had been presented to him by a lady missionary. But as he stepped inside, the head waiter's eye fell upon his frayed trousers and decadent shoes.
paragraphs.zh: 苏比对自己背心最下面一颗纽扣以上的部分信心十足。他刮了脸，外套还算体面，整洁的黑领结是一位教会女布道士送的。然而他刚迈进门槛，领班领座那双锐利的眼睛就落到了他磨破的裤脚和寒酸的破鞋上。

paragraphs.en: Strong and ready hands turned him about and conveyed him in silence and haste to the sidewalk and averted the ignoble fate of the menaced mallard. Soapy turned off Broadway. It seemed that his route to the coveted island was not to be an easy one.
paragraphs.zh: 一双强壮敏捷的大手敏捷地将他转了个身，悄无声息而又迅疾地将他推到了人行道上，及时化解了一只濒危烤鸭的不幸宿命。苏比讪讪地拐出百老汇。看来，通往心仪小岛的道路并非一帆风顺。

paragraphs.en: At a corner of Sixth Avenue electric lights displayed shop merchandise behind plate glass. Soapy took a stone and dashed it through the glass. People came running around the corner, a policeman in the lead.
paragraphs.zh: 在第六大道的一个街角，璀璨的电灯映照着大块平板玻璃橱窗里的精美商品。苏比拾起一块石头，狠狠砸向了玻璃。人们纷纷从街角跑来，一位巡警一马当先冲在最前面。

paragraphs.en: Soapy stood still, with his hands in his pockets, and smiled at the sight of brass buttons. 'Where's the man that done that?' inquired the officer excitedly. 'Don't you figure out that I might have had something to do with it?' said Soapy, not without sarcasm.
paragraphs.zh: 苏比双手插兜站在原地一动不动，看到黄铜警钮露出了从容的微笑。“是谁干的？”警官气喘吁吁地盘问。“难道你看不出我跟这事脱不了干系吗？”苏比带着一丝嘲讽回答道。

paragraphs.en: The policeman's mind refused to accept Soapy even as a clue. Men who smash windows do not remain to parley with the law's minions. They take to their heels. The policeman saw a man halfway down the block running to catch a car. With drawn club he joined in the pursuit. Soapy, with disgust in his heart, walked slowly on.
paragraphs.zh: 巡警的脑筋甚至拒绝把苏比列为怀疑对象。砸碎橱窗的罪犯绝不会留下来跟警界喽啰攀谈闲扯，他们早就脚底抹油溜之大吉了。巡警瞥见半条街外有个男人正在奔跑追赶电车，便拔出警棍一路猛追而去。苏比满心晦气与嫌恶，慢腾腾地继续往前溜达。

paragraphs.en: On the opposite side of the street was a restaurant of no great pretensions. It catered to large appetites and modest purses. Into this Soapy took his accursed shoes and telltale trousers without challenge.
paragraphs.zh: 在街道对面有一家门面不起眼的小餐馆。它专门照顾大胃口与浅荷包的食客。苏比拖着他那双该死的破鞋和破绽百出的裤子大摇大摆走进去，竟毫无阻拦。

paragraphs.en: At a table he sat and consumed beefsteak, flapjacks and doughnut and pie. And then to the waiter he betrayed the fact that the minutest coin and himself were total strangers. 'Now, get busy and call a cop,' said Soapy. 'And don't keep a gentleman waiting.'
paragraphs.zh: 他在一张餐桌前坐下，狼吞虎咽地吃下了牛排、热薄饼、甜甜圈和馅饼。随后，他向侍者坦白了一个事实：哪怕世上最小的一枚硬币，跟他也是素不相识的陌生人。“好了，快去叫警察吧，”苏比说，“别让一位绅士久等。”

paragraphs.en: 'No cop for youse,' said the waiter, with a voice like butter cakes and an eye like the cherry in a Manhattan cocktail. 'Hey, Con!' Neatly upon his left ear on the callous pavement two waiters pitched Soapy. He arose, joint by joint, as a carpenter's rule opens, and beat the dust from his clothes.
paragraphs.zh: “叫警察太便宜你了，”侍者用黄油蛋糕般油腻的嗓门说，眼睛凶神恶煞得像曼哈顿鸡尾酒里的樱桃，“喂，康！”两名跑堂合力把苏比像掷铁饼一样，左耳贴地狠狠扔在冰冷坚硬的人行道上。苏比像一把折尺似的一节一节撑起身来，拍落衣服上的尘土。

paragraphs.en: A policeman who stood before a drugstore two doors away laughed and walked down the street. Soapy was seized with a panic that some dreadful enchantment had rendered him immune to arrest.
paragraphs.zh: 两家店开外站在药房门口的巡警看了哈哈大笑，转身溜达走了。苏比突然陷入了一阵莫名的恐慌：仿佛有一道邪恶的魔咒笼罩着他，让他永远对被捕免疫。

paragraphs.en: He traveled on and reached another stretch where the avenues were broad and brilliantly lighted. In front of a theatre he noticed a young woman of modest and pleasant appearance looking at the posters. The policeman was leaning against a water plug three paces away.
paragraphs.zh: 他继续向前走，来到一片马路宽阔、街灯璀璨的繁华地带。一家剧院门前，他注意到一位衣着朴素文静的年轻女子正在看海报。三步开外，一位巡警正惬意地倚着消防栓。

paragraphs.en: It was Soapy's design to assume the role of the despicable and loathed 'masher.' His hair was smoothed, his cravat adjusted, and he approached the young woman with a jaunty swagger. 'Ah there, Bedelia! Don't you want to come and play in my yard?'
paragraphs.zh: 苏比打算扮演一个令人鄙夷作呕的街头浪荡登徒子。他抹平头发，正了正领带，神气活现地踱到年轻女子跟前。“嗨，贝黛莉亚！要不要跟我到后院玩玩呀？”

paragraphs.en: The young woman turned, looked at him, and smilingly stepped close to his side. 'Sure, Mike,' she said joyfully, 'if you'll blow me to a beer. I'd have spoke to you sooner, but the cop was looking.' She hooked her arm affectionately into Soapy's.
paragraphs.zh: 年轻女子回过头打量了他一眼，嫣然一笑，亲昵地贴了上来。“好啊，迈克，”她兴高采烈地说，“只要你请我喝杯啤酒。我本来早就想找你搭话了，只是刚才那警察一直盯着呢。”说着，她深情款款地挽住了苏比的手臂。

paragraphs.en: The policeman was still looking. Soapy, with feelings akin to horror, freed himself from his companion and ran blindly. At the next corner he began to yell drunken gibberish at the top of his harsh voice. He danced, howled, raved and otherwise disturbed the welkin.
paragraphs.zh: 巡警依然朝这边看着。苏比吓得魂飞魄散，拼命挣脱了女伴的手臂落荒而逃。在下一个拐角处，他扯开破锣般的嗓门，像疯汉一样大吵大嚷，手舞足蹈，怪叫狂号，把宁静的夜空吵得天翻地覆。

paragraphs.en: The policeman twirled his club, turned his back to Soapy and remarked to a citizen: ''Tis one of them Yale lads celebratin' the goose egg they give to the Hartford College. Noisy; but no harm. We've instructions to leave 'em be.'
paragraphs.zh: 巡警转动着警棍，转过身背对着苏比，向身边的一位市民解释道：“这是耶鲁大学的小伙子们在庆祝击败哈特福德学院呢。吵是吵了点，但没啥恶意。上头有指令，由着他们闹腾去吧。”

paragraphs.en: Disconsolate, Soapy ceased his unavailing racket. Would never a policeman lay hands on him? In his fancy the Island seemed an unattainable Arcadia. He buttoned his thin coat against the chilling wind.
paragraphs.zh: 苏比心灰意冷，停止了徒劳的叫闹。难道真的没有警察肯碰他一根汗毛吗？在他幻觉中，小岛监狱俨然成了遥不可及的世外桃源。他扣紧了单薄的外套，抵御刺骨的寒风。

paragraphs.en: In a cigar store he saw a well-dressed man lighting a cigar at a swinging light. His silk umbrella he had set by the door on entering. Soapy stepped inside, took the umbrella and sauntered off with it slowly. The man at the cigar light followed hastily.
paragraphs.zh: 在一家雪茄烟店里，他看见一位衣着讲究的男士正在悬吊的火苗前点雪茄。进门时他把一把真丝雨伞倚在了门边。苏比溜进店里，顺手抄起雨伞，慢条斯理地踱了出去。点烟的男人急忙追了出来。

paragraphs.en: 'My umbrella,' he said, sternly. 'Oh, is it?' sneered Soapy, adding insult to petit larceny. 'Well, why don't you call a policeman? I took it. Your umbrella! Why don't you call a cop? There stands one on the corner.'
paragraphs.zh: “那是我的伞！”男人严厉喝道。“噢，是吗？”苏比冷嘲热讽，在偷窃之余更添挑衅，“那好啊，你干嘛不叫警察？是我拿的。你的伞！干嘛不叫警察？拐角处就站着一个呢。”

paragraphs.en: The umbrella owner slowed his steps. 'Of course,' said he, 'that is—well, you know how these mistakes occur—I—if it's your umbrella I hope you'll excuse me—I picked it up this morning in a restaurant—if you recognize it as yours, why—I hope you'll—'
paragraphs.zh: 雨伞的主人反而放慢了脚步，支吾起来：“当然……我是说……您知道难免会有这种误会……如果这是您的伞，我请您多包涵……我今天早上在一家餐馆里顺手拿的……既然您认出是您的，那……我真希望您……”

paragraphs.en: 'Of course it's mine,' said Soapy, viciously. The ex-umbrella man retreated. The policeman hurried to assist a tall blonde across the street in front of a street car. Soapy hurled the umbrella into an excavation.
paragraphs.zh: “那当然是我的！”苏比恶狠狠地说道。前任伞主仓皇退缩了。巡警则急匆匆跑去护送一位金发高个女郎穿越电车轨道。苏比气急败坏地把雨伞狠狠砸进了一个大深坑里。

paragraphs.en: He walked eastward through a street damaged by improvements. At an unusually quiet corner Soapy came to a standstill. Here was an old church, quaint and rambling and gabled. Through one violet-stained window a soft light glowed, where no doubt the organist loitered over the keys, making sure of his mastery of the coming Sabbath anthem.
paragraphs.zh: 他沿着一条正在修路的破损街道向东走去。在一个格外僻静安宁的街角，苏比停住了脚步。这里坐落着一座古老的教堂，古朴典雅、山墙高耸。透过一扇紫罗兰色的彩色玻璃窗，一缕柔和的灯光倾泻而出，风琴师显然正在琴键前练习，为即将到来的安息日赞美诗做最后的准备。

paragraphs.en: For there drifted out to Soapy's ear sweet music that caught and held him transfixed against the convolutions of the iron fence. The moon was above, lustrous and serene; vehicles and pedestrians were few; sparrows twittered sleepily in the eaves—and the anthem cemented Soapy to the iron rail.
paragraphs.zh: 一阵悠扬圣洁的乐声飘入苏比的耳畔，将他牢牢定格在精美的铁栅栏旁。明月高悬，皎洁而静谧；车马与行人都已寥寥；屋檐下的麻雀发出倦怠的啼鸣——赞美诗仿佛施了魔法，将苏比紧扣在栏杆前。

paragraphs.en: For he had known it well in the days when his life contained such things as mothers and roses and ambitions and friends and immaculate thoughts and collars. The conjunction of Soapy's receptive state of mind and the influences about the old church wrought a sudden and wonderful change in his soul.
paragraphs.zh: 在往昔美好的岁月里，他曾无比熟悉这首赞美诗，那时他的生活里还有母亲、玫瑰、壮志、挚友，以及一尘不染的思想与洁净的衣领。此刻苏比柔软敞开的心灵与古老教堂的神圣氛围交融碰撞，在他的灵魂深处激起了一场奇迹般的剧变。

paragraphs.en: He viewed with swift horror the pit into which he had tumbled, the degraded days, unworthy desires, dead hopes, wrecked faculties and base motives that made up his existence. And also in a moment his heart responded thrillingly to this new mood.
paragraphs.zh: 他惊恐万状地俯瞰自己堕入的深渊：那些沉沦堕落的岁月、卑鄙无耻的欲望、幻灭死去的希望、支离破碎的才智以及构成他苟且人生的低下动机。就在这同一瞬间，他的心怦然而动，迸发出强烈的渴望与新生。

paragraphs.en: A sudden impulse moved him to battle with his desperate fate. He would pull himself out of the mire; he would make a man of himself again; he would conquer the evil that had enslaved him. There was time; he was young yet; he would resurrect his old eager ambitions and pursue them without faltering.
paragraphs.zh: 一股强大的冲动促使他奋起抗争绝望的宿命。他要将自己从泥潭中拔出来；他要重新堂堂正正做人；他要战胜奴役他的邪恶诱惑！时间还来得及，他还年轻！他要复活往昔热切的雄心壮志，义无反顾地勇往直前！

paragraphs.en: Those solemn but sweet organ notes had set up a revolution in him. Tomorrow he would go into the roaring downtown district and find work. A fur importer had once offered him a place as driver. He would find him tomorrow and ask for the position. He would be somebody in the world. He would—
paragraphs.zh: 那些庄严肃穆而又婉转甜美的琴音在他胸中掀起了一场革命。明天他就要去繁华的商业区找工作。曾有一位皮货进口商想雇他当司机，明天他一定要找到那人应聘。他要在人世间出人头地！他要——

paragraphs.en: Soapy felt a hand laid on his arm. He looked quickly around into the broad face of a policeman. 'What are you doin' here?' asked the officer. 'Nothin',' said Soapy. 'Then come along,' said the policeman. 'Three months on the Island,' said the Magistrate in the Police Court the next morning.
paragraphs.zh: 苏比感到一只手沉重地搭在了他的胳膊上。他猛地回头，迎面撞上一位巡警圆阔的面孔。“你在这儿鬼鬼祟祟干什么？”警官盘问道。“没干什么，”苏比轻声说。“那就跟我走一趟吧，”巡警说。第二天早晨，警察法庭的法官判决道：“去岛上服刑三个月。”
